references.text: Moses predicts that Israel will turn to other gods after being satisfied in the promised land, which directly connects to the description of Jeshurun becoming fat and kicking.
Another occurrence of the name Jeshurun as a poetic designation for Israel.
Jeshurun is mentioned again, and God is described as Israel's helper and savior.
Isaiah uses the name Jeshurun as an affectionate term for Israel, in contrast to the apostate people in Deuteronomy.
Hosea describes how Israel became satisfied and then forgot the Lord, a direct echo of the theme in Deuteronomy 32:15.
Nehemiah recounts Israel's history and describes how they grew fat and enjoyed God's blessings, yet still rebelled against Him.
The psalm describes how Israel was filled with food, yet turned away from God in their abundance.
The Rock of Israel's salvation is mentioned, a theme repeated as 'the rock of my salvation' in Deuteronomy 32:15.
God is described as our rock of salvation, the same image used in Deuteronomy 32:15.
